title: Modelling N2O emissions in fertilized grasslands with machine learning: a multi-site LSTM approach
content:
Modelling N2O emissions in fertilized grasslands with machine learning: a multi-site LSTM approach
Samin Payrosangari, Kathrin Fuchs, Benjamin Wolf, Ralf Kiese, and Clemens Scheer
Biogeosciences, 23, 8341–8360, https://doi.org/10.5194/bg-23-8341-2026, 2026
We implemented a LSTM (long short-term memory) model to improve the simulation of daily N2O emissions at regional scale across several pre-alpine grasslands in Central Europe. The study focuses on evaluating the model’s applicability to cross-site grasslands in the region. This work contributes to the development of regional N₂O emission models, thereby reducing the effort required to estimate emissions from sites lacking direct measurements.

title: Oxygen Dynamics Across Connected Coastal Ecosystems: Heterogeneity May Mitigate Oxygen Extremes
content:
Abstract
Dissolved oxygen (DO) circulates biogeochemically among the atmosphere, hydrosphere, and biosphere, serving as an important indicator of ecosystem functioning in coastal ecosystems. Coral reefs, seagrass beds, and mangroves frequently co‐occur in tropical coastal zones, but how oxygen dynamics connect these adjacent ecosystems remains poorly resolved. Here, high‐frequency observations across connected coral reef, seagrass, and mangrove systems were conducted to examine spatial and temporal variability in DO regimes. DO dynamics differed among the three adjacent ecosystems. DO variability in the coral reef and seagrass bed was dominated by diel periodicity, whereas mangrove DO fluctuations were primarily structured by semidiurnal tidal variability, with an additional diel component. Maximum DO saturation reached 172% in the coral reef, 162% in the seagrass bed, and 146% in the mangrove, while hypoxic conditions developed in the mangrove, where DO declined to 19.9%. Supersaturation occurred during 44.7% and 51.7% of the observation period in the coral reef and seagrass bed, respectively, with events persisting for up to 21 hr. Multivariate analyses and statistical modeling revealed environmental controls on oxygen dynamics and ecosystem‐specific differences among adjacent ecosystems. Notably, water temperature emerged as a consistently important correlate of oxygen dynamics across ecosystems. Spatial heterogeneity in oxygen dynamics emerged across connected coastal ecosystems, forming an oxygen patchwork that may mitigate local oxygen extremes associated with hypoxia and hyperoxia. This study positions oxygen as an integrative proxy for detecting cross‐ecosystem functional linkages.

title: Hybrid Spectral Downscaling of Directional Wave Spectra in the Gulf of Panama: Seasonal Organization and Transformation of Offshore Wave Systems
content:
Abstract
Global wave reanalyzes characterize offshore sea states, but their application in shallow and semi‐enclosed basins is limited by insufficient resolution of coastal geometry, bathymetry, and local wind forcing. Directional wave spectra are reconstructed for the Gulf of Panama, a representative semi‐enclosed basin of the eastern tropical Pacific, using a hybrid framework trained on Simulating WAves Nearshore (SWAN) simulations. ERA5 offshore conditions were propagated through two complementary metamodel components representing swell propagation and locally generated wind sea, yielding continuous spectra for 1969–2023 at 100 stations. Validation against SWAN showed good agreement for significant wave height, peak period, and mean direction. The reconstructed spectra reveal offshore‐to‐inner‐gulf gradients in spectral energy and directional structure, driven by coexisting offshore wave systems (WS) and the combined bathymetric and geometric control on wave transformation and directional filtering. Seasonal clustering identified 13 dry‐season (December–April) and 8 wet‐season (May–November) wave‐spectral microregions, with the dry season characterized by bimodality and crossed‐sea conditions and the wet season by a meridional structure dominated by Southern Hemisphere swell. Within these microregions, dominant variability reflects energy modulation, while secondary modes capture spectral reorganization through directional rotation and frequency redistribution. The three main offshore WS remain identifiable throughout the basin but undergo progressive reorientation and selective filtering landward, while systems generated by local controls emerge recurrently toward the inner gulf. These results show that waves within the Gulf of Panama exhibit a spatially and spectrally structured organization that is only partly captured by bulk parameters, with implications for coastal erosion and flood‐risk assessment.

title: Rapid Winter Mixed‐Layer Deepening Linked to Sea Ice Breakup in the Beaufort Sea
content:
Abstract
Winter storms in the Beaufort Sea can trigger large‐scale sea ice breakup, opening leads and enhancing ice mobility. These events can influence the mixed layer through various processes, like brine rejection and shear‐driven mixing. However, their relative importance remains unclear due to limited observations. We investigate the upper ocean response to a major breakup event in February–March 2013, during which three ice‐tethered profilers recorded rapid mixed‐layer deepening. We use these observations in conjunction with a regional coupled ice‐ocean model and a single‐column mixed‐layer model to analyze the driving mechanisms. The regional model confirms that the observed deepening is widespread and anomalous in the region and coincides with the breakup. The single‐column model experiments suggest local brine rejection and shear stress play a minor role. Instead, both the regional model and observation‐based estimates of Ekman pumping indicate that the primary mechanism of the deepening is large‐scale downwelling, driven by increased stress input as ice drifts more freely. This contrasts with the typical winter regime, where thick and compact sea ice inhibits downwelling. We discuss how more frequent breakup events in a weakening ice cover could impact freshwater storage in the Beaufort Sea, a process likely underestimated in current climate models.

title: Mixed Layer Depth (MLD) and Barrier Layer Thickness (BLT) Influence Vertical Profiles of PAHs in the South China Sea
content:
Abstract
Semi‐volatile organic contaminants (SVOCs), such as polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), may exhibit different spatial distribution and environmental behaviors in marine environments, which depend on various oceanic processes. This study examined the spatial distribution and depth profile of dissolved PAHs in the marginal South China Sea (SCS). The PAH concentrations in the SCS, ranging from 4.7 to 50 ng L−1 on average, were dominated by two‐ring compounds nearshore and shifted toward three‐ and four‐ring compounds offshore, with higher concentrations found in the northwestern and western SCS and extremely low concentrations found in the northeastern and central SCS. For the depth profile, several physical layers, including mixed layer depth (MLD) and barrier layer thickness (BLT), were calculated. The concentration of PAHs on the surface was inversely correlated with the proximity to the nearest landmasses. The distribution in subsurface water layers, however, was influenced by eddy diffusion, coastal upwelling, Kuroshio Current incursion, etc. As a result of their severity, coastal upwelling and atmospheric impacts led to higher PAH levels in the MLD. Meanwhile, the northeastern SCS displayed relatively high levels in the deep layer (DL) because of the rapid vertical fluxes by eddy diffusion. The presence of stratified BLT layers, which effectively trapped PAHs originating from subsurface water mass with slower eddy diffusion from the surface, can be attributed to the sandwich‐like pattern of the SCS.

title: Targeted eDNA Detects Spatial Patterns of Mitochondrial Lineages Across Hydrological Seasons in the Yangtze Finless Porpoise
content:
ABSTRACT
Seasonal variation in habitat connectivity can influence the spatial distribution of mobile aquatic populations. However, tracking these effects in fine‐scale mitochondrial lineage patterns is challenging because conventional monitoring often relies on invasive biopsy or opportunistic tissue sampling. Environmental DNA (eDNA) provides a non‐invasive alternative, but whether it can resolve spatial lineage‐associated signals under natural hydrological fluctuations remains unclear. We combined a tissue‐derived mitochondrial reference with targeted eDNA amplicon sequencing using a diagnostic mitochondrial single‐nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) panel to assess spatial patterns in mitochondrial lineage‐associated eDNA of the critically endangered Yangtze finless porpoise (Neophocaena asiaeorientalis) across the Poyang Lake floodplain under contrasting hydrological conditions. Wet‐season detection was limited, precluding comparable assessment of spatial lineage patterns. During the normal‐season survey, spatial heterogeneity of lineage‐associated eDNA was detected, and Clade A relative read abundance (RRA) covaried with the distribution of several benthic prey taxa. During dry‐season water recession, comparable regional differentiation was not detected and available aquatic habitats were more restricted. During the normal season, eDNA‐derived lineage patterns broadly reflected regional patterns in tissue samples. A conservation‐priority matrix combining the Shannon index of lineage‐associated eDNA RRA with quantitative PCR (qPCR)‐derived eDNA concentration identified sites with above‐median eDNA concentrations and relatively even representation of the two mitochondrial lineages. These findings indicate that targeted eDNA may extend non‐invasive monitoring beyond species detection by adding lineage‐level information to conservation planning under dynamic hydrological conditions.

title: Epigenetic Clocks Uncover the Natural History of Ageing in Wild Mice
content:
ABSTRACT
Environmental stressors are expected to accelerate senescence but demonstrating this requires both a measure of senescence and knowledge of chronological age—data rarely available for most wild animals. Here, we constructed a DNA methylation‐based epigenetic clock for the wood mouse (Apodemus sylvaticus) using known‐aged laboratory individuals and applied it to a wild population of unknown ages. This represents one of the first demonstrations that a laboratory‐trained epigenetic clock can be used to infer age structure in free‐living animals. Multiple lines of evidence validated use of the clock in wild individuals: age estimates fell within expected ranges, recapitulated population demographic structure, and recovered predicted signatures of senescence, including an increase in infection probability with age. Moreover, wild mice given experimental food supplementation and parasite‐removal drugs exhibited slower epigenetic ageing rates. Together, our findings demonstrate that epigenetic clocks can infer both chronological age and ageing rates in the wild, providing a powerful framework to identify the ecological and individual determinants of ageing.

title: Local adaptation expands genetic variation in the thermal performance of a coastal fish: Implications for ocean warming
content:
Abstract
Species' responses to climate change can include a component of contemporary evolution, and such responses can be important in offsetting the detrimental effects of warming. However, the capacity of populations to evolve will depend on the level of genetic variation underlying traits affected by climate change. It is not always clear how such variation is maintained, but one plausible mechanism involves adaptation of subpopulations to local climate conditions. In this study, we experimentally tested whether populations of a coastal fish, the California Grunion, exhibited inherited differences in thermal reaction norms (measured as the family‐average values of growth and mortality across a range of temperatures). We also quantified the degree to which differentiation among locations increased the amount of genetic variation underlying thermal reaction norms within the population at large. We collected gametes from three local populations that were separated by an average of 150 km and located along a north–south cline. Eggs from each population were fertilized in a breeding experiment that allowed us to quantify genetic variation and heritability. Larvae from all three populations were reared in a common laboratory environment and across temperatures reflecting their natural range. Patterns of growth exhibited inherited differences in that offspring from higher latitude populations grew faster on average when reared in identical conditions. Offspring from different source populations varied significantly in how sensitive their mortality rates were to temperature, and offspring from parents in the lowest latitude population had lower mortality rates at high temperatures. When growth and mortality rates were combined to express biomass, we saw evidence of both counter gradient variation (greater production from high‐latitude populations) and local adaptation in thermal specialization (peak production occurred at higher temperatures for the lowest latitude population). Genetic variation among locations increased the total amount of genetic variation within the broader metapopulation. Even when considering only three subpopulations, broad‐sense heritability values were increased for both growth and mortality rate by factors of 1.07 and 1.1, respectively. Our results emphasize that metapopulation‐level processes can play important roles in both the promotion of genetic variation and the response to selection generated by climate change.

title: Conserved Upper Thermal Limits and Small Safety Margins in Soil Copiotrophic Bacteria
content:
To evaluate the role of phylogeny and the environment in shaping thermal performance curves of copiotrophic bacteria from soil, we sampled bacterial isolates across top‐soils from different environments in California. Differences in thermal traits follow phylogeny, whereas environmental variables explain only a minimal fraction of the variance. Overall, we observed constrained evolution of thermal curves with sharp decreases in growth above 38°C for Pseudomonadales and 40°C for Enterobacterales.

ABSTRACT
One of the key uncertainties in climate change models is how microbes will adapt to rising temperatures. Large‐scale comparisons of bacterial thermal performances show a clear boundary between mesophiles and thermophiles. Here, we investigated whether phylogenetic constraints limit the adaptive potential of bacteria to warming soils. Focusing on copiotrophs within Gammaproteobacteria (N = 251 isolates across 18 genera), we found that both thermal optima and upper thermal limits are constrained; variation in these traits decreases above 40°C across the phylogeny, with minimal influence of present‐day bioclimatic variables. This, along with the reduced thermal safety margins found in fluctuating hot climates, suggests that many isolates may already be maladapted to local temperature variability. Our findings indicate that these constraints interact with the geometry of thermal performance curves, imposing a trade‐off between high‐temperature performance and the risk of substantial fitness losses above Topt. Overall, this work underscores potential limits to thermal adaptation and their implications for bacterial fitness.

title: Neuronal XOR computation requires temporally activated synaptic information
content:
by Yanheng Li, Xiaojuan Sun, Yunliang Zang

Single neurons can perform complex exclusive-or (XOR) computation which is conventionally thought to need multilayer networks, yet the biophysical mechanisms and the robustness of such computations under stochastic synaptic drive remain unclear. Using biologically realistic modeling, we demonstrate that dendritic depolarization block provides a universal and robust mechanism for XOR-like computation. Voltage-gated calcium channels enable a non-monotonic input-output relationship: moderate asynchronous drive evokes spiking, whereas excessive drive induces a sustained plateau that suppresses output, naturally implementing XOR logic computation. This computation is strictly gated by temporal distribution of synaptic inputs rather than spatial distribution; the XOR-like response is robust across diverse dendritic configurations but collapses under synchronous activation. Dendritic depolarization block propagates to the soma via dendrite-soma coupling, establishing a neuronal output-limiting mechanism. The computation is highly efficient, leveraging a frequency–synapse-count trade-off to ensure stable logic operations across varying levels of background activity. Cross-morphological validation confirms that XOR-like computation is morphology-independent, representing a generalizable biophysical principle of neural information processing.

title: Epidemic control under incomplete observations through mechanistic state reconstruction and multi-agent learning
content:
by Shang Wang, Yuxiao Luo, Yunduan Cui, Meng Zhang, Min Kang, Ling Yin

Epidemic-control policies are usually optimized from reported infection states, but these reports are often incomplete because testing capacity, reporting behavior, delays, and asymptomatic infections vary across regions and time. Such observation gaps can distort the state used by the controller and lead to suboptimal testing and isolation decisions. We develop a three-stage computational epidemiology framework that links observation modeling, state reconstruction, and policy optimization. First, we extend a metapopulation SEIQR model to represent fully observable, steady partially observable, and non-steady partially observable surveillance regimes. Second, we introduce ODE-DynNet, a hybrid reconstruction model that combines mobility-coupled epidemic dynamics with graph-temporal learning to infer hidden infection states from distorted observations. Third, we formulate coordinated testing and isolation as a multi-agent reinforcement learning problem with a flow-based responsibility-aware reward that attributes transmission costs across connected regions. Using community-level mobility data from Shenzhen, China, we show that ODE-DynNet reduces infection cost by 88% (from 4,930 to 590) relative to the non-steady partially observable, decoupled policy that uses the raw proxy without reconstruction. The same pipeline remains effective across transmission intensities and reporting-delay settings, indicating that explicit observation modeling and state reconstruction are useful preprocessing steps for learned epidemic-control policies under incomplete surveillance.

title: A flexible agent-based modelling framework of multi-serotype pneumococcal carriage to evaluate vaccine strategies in large populations
content:
by Nefel Tellioglu, David J. Price, Xinghui Chen, Violeta Spirkoska, Cyan Yingying Wang, Robert Moss, Natalie Carvalho, Kylie S. Carville, Patricia Therese Campbell, Jodie McVernon

Streptococcus pneumoniae is a multi-serotype pathogen causing a substantial global burden of pneumonia and invasive bacterial disease. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines have been implemented worldwide, protecting against colonisation and disease from selected high-burden serotypes, but in many settings short-term effectiveness has been eroded by serotype replacement. Vaccines with broader serotype coverage have been developed, at the cost of immunogenicity against single serotypes. To determine the longer-term impact of these new formulations, we propose a novel modelling framework that evaluates the relationship between serotype-specific vaccine immunogenicity and effectiveness, comprising immunity, carriage and clinical models. Dynamics of individual serotypes are modelled over time, advancing existing modelling paradigms that group all serotypes according to vaccine type. This framework is sufficiently flexible to consider diverse populations, emerging vaccine formulations and implementation strategies. A retrospective analysis of sequential introduction of 7- and 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccines in Australia demonstrates the flexibility of the model.

title: Robust parametric estimation of avian cranial morphology
content:
by Kaikwan Lau, Gary P. T. Choi

Quantifying morphology from 3D scans is increasingly central to comparative biology, yet many existing pipelines require labor-intensive manual landmarking and impose strict assumptions on the data quality, hindering the high-throughput analysis of large and often imperfect digitized collections. In this work, we develop a fully unsupervised geometric framework that extracts robust parametric descriptors of cranial morphology directly from imperfect 3D skull meshes. Specifically, utilizing tools in computational geometry, differential geometry, and numerical optimization, the framework automatically aligns each specimen, measures the primary skull dimensions, and fits geometric primitives to the orbit and the neurocranium via robust iterative schemes, yielding stable estimates even for topologically noisy or damaged meshes. We demonstrate the framework on 100 skull specimens of Darwin’s finches and their relatives. The extracted measurements recover the well-established scaling relationship between skull size and orbit curvature, providing a biological validation of the automated pipeline. Building on this, we establish a predictive model that estimates the orbit curvature from three easily obtainable linear skull measurements, explaining 86.36% of the variance in curvature with an average prediction error of only 6.14%, and further derive dimensionless relative-geometry descriptors that are invariant to uniform scaling and retain variation among the sampled genera. We also demonstrate the generalizability of our method by applying it to other avian and mammalian skulls. Altogether, our work establishes a rigorous foundation for the digital estimation and high-throughput phenotyping of large-scale museum collections without the need for manual landmarking.

title: Ten simple rules for creating and maintaining FAIR competency frameworks
content:
by Denise Bianco, Daria Sokolova, Matthew Forshaw, Clementina Ramirez Marengo, Emma Karoune, Kim T. Gurwitz, Vera Matser

In a modern skills-based economy, competency frameworks are essential tools for workforce planning, career progression, and professional development. However, traditional frameworks often exist as static, isolated documents that lack digital connectivity and machine-readability. This article introduces a strategic roadmap to modernise professional standards by applying the FAIR principles: making competency frameworks Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable. We present the FAIR competency framework lifecycle, an iterative model centred on end-user engagement, and outline 10 simple rules to guide creators through every stage of development. These rules cover foundational definitions, clear language, persistent identifiers, permissive licensing, and robust governance. By turning frameworks into machine-actionable digital objects, organisations can ensure their standards are easily discoverable, reusable, and ready to integrate into broader learning management systems. Ultimately, adopting these guidelines promotes a more interconnected, transparent, and adaptable global skills landscape where professional expertise can be recognised and shared efficiently.

title: Allosteric inhibition rescues hydrocephalus caused by catalytically inactive Shp2 in mice
content:
by Neoklis Makrides, Emily Sun, Hilal Mir, Jen-Zen Chuang, Ziyuan Jiang, Yihua Wu, Carlos Serra, John Peregrin, Qian Wang, Wellington V. Cardoso, Ching-Hwa Sung, Neel H. Shah, Xin Zhang

SHP2, a protein tyrosine phosphatase (PTP) crucial in Ras-MAPK signaling, is associated with various human congenital diseases and cancers. Here, we show that the catalytically inactive Shp2C459S mutation results in communicating hydrocephalus, similar to the catalytically activating Shp2E76K and Mek1DD mutants. Unlike previous mutants, however, Shp2C459S/+ mutation uniquely affects ciliary development rather than neurogenesis, leading to structural abnormalities in cilia and impaired ciliary motility. Differential scanning fluorimetry suggested that SHP2C459S, SHP2E76K, and SHP2C459S/E76K mutations all induce an open SHP2 conformation, but only SHP2C459S leads to aberrant GAB1 phosphorylation in cells expressing wild-type SHP2. Consistent with this distinct signaling profile, brain ventricular tissues from Shp2C459S/+ mice exhibit elevated GAB1 and AKT phosphorylation despite normal ERK and STAT3 activities, implicating dysregulated PI3K–AKT signaling in the pathogenesis of hydrocephalus. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of PI3K markedly rescues ciliogenesis defects and alleviates hydrocephalus in mutant mice. Furthermore, the allosteric SHP2 inhibitor SHP099 increases the thermal stability of SHP2C459S protein, consistent with a shift toward a closed state, and ameliorates hydrocephalus in Shp2C459S/+ mice. These findings suggest that, in this engineered mouse model, Shp2-associated hydrocephalus is driven by conformational changes rather than altered catalytic activity. Our results underscore the therapeutic potential of conformation-specific allosteric inhibitors in targeting both catalytically active and inactive SHP2 mutants.

title: Dissipation‐Decoupling‐Reorganization: Three Layer Response and Energy Matter Decoupling in the Urban Boundary Layer to Anthropogenic Heating
content:
Abstract
Coherent structure contributions to momentum, sensible heat, and CO2 fluxes after anthropogenic heating were examined based on seven level turbulence observations from the Beijing 325 m meteorological tower. A three layer vertical structure was identified according to the 2017 data set: a near surface dissipation layer (8–15 m) marked by reduced CO2 transport efficiency, organized coherent structures decreased significantly; a decoupling layer (47–80 m) characterized by divergent responses in the ejection and sweep contributions to heat and CO2 fluxes; and an upper reorganization layer (200–280 m) featuring with recovered transport efficiency and a profile inflection point. This three layer pattern is most clearly expressed in 2017. Data from 2016 to 2015 show simplified two layer (decoupling and reorganization) without a distinct dissipation layer, indicating that the complete three layer response depends on background meteorological conditions. Our results provide a vertically explicit framework for understanding anthropogenic perturbations to urban turbulence transport process.

title: From Qualitative to Quantitative: A Data‐Driven Error Budget for Satellite Water Vapor Product Bias
content:
Abstract
Satellite‐derived precipitable water vapor (PWV) products are widely used for meteorological and climatological research, yet the relative contributions of environmental and observational variables to product uncertainties remain unquantified. Here, we present an explainable machine‐learning framework that integrates extreme gradient boosting with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to establish a data‐driven error budget for satellite PWV product bias. The model accurately characterizes nonlinear relationships between product bias and multiple influencing factors, with an R2 of 0.70, an RMSE of 2.19 mm, and an MAE of 1.57 mm. The SHAP‐based error budget reveals that background atmospheric moisture is the dominant contributor (29.69%), followed by surface temperature (14.27%), latitude (11.35%), and longitude (9.34%). Moving beyond previous qualitative evaluations, this framework provides a quantitative decomposition of satellite PWV product bias into multiple environmental and observational variables. The approach can be adapted to other evaluation metrics and extended to other satellite‐derived water vapor and geophysical products.

title: Controls of Radiocarbon in Dissolved Organic Carbon in the Southwestern Indian Ocean
content:
Abstract
The Southwestern Indian Ocean is a hydrographically and geologically complex area featuring prominent upwelling and deep basins separated by mid‐ocean ridges. Radiocarbon content (Δ14C) of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) was measured at three stations (24°S–3°S). In the intermediate layer (200–1,500 m), a multiple linear regression (MLR) model using salinity, temperature, and apparent oxygen utilization demonstrated that conservative water mass mixing predominantly controls DOC Δ14C variability. In the deep layer (>2,000 m), a northward decline in DOC Δ14C values was not reproduced by MLR predictions. This pattern may partly reflect varying contributions of Circumpolar Deep Water and Indian Deep Water, combined with addition of aged DOC or selective removal of younger DOC. Older radiocarbon signatures of DOC were associated with elevated δ3He, suggesting an influence from hydrothermal processes.

title: Ecosystem Responsiveness Diverges From Environmental Variability Across Alpine Ecosystems
content:
Abstract
Environmental variability is widely assumed to govern ecosystem responses, yet how GPP response magnitude varies with environmental forcing remains unclear. Using ecosystem sensitivity experiments across the Tibetan Plateau, we quantified overall effective gross primary productivity (GPP) responsiveness and composite environmental forcing variability along the elevation gradient. The results showed that environmental forcing variability increased toward high elevations, whereas overall effective GPP responsiveness exhibited a maximum at lower‐mid elevations. This divergence demonstrates that greater environmental fluctuations do not necessarily correspond to a greater GPP response under observed forcing. Maximum responsiveness occurred in transitional environments where moderate forcing variability coincided with relatively strong GPP responses. Comparisons with alternative GPP products showed a broadly consistent pattern, providing corroborating evidence. Our findings highlight the importance of considering both forcing variability and ecosystem responsiveness when identifying regions where carbon uptake responds strongly to environmental change.

title: Novel Constraints on Groundwater Flow in Fractured Systems by Combining Isotopic, Hydrochemical, and Microbial Tracers
content:
Abstract
Groundwater in mountainous areas plays a critical role in sustaining regional water resources and ecosystem stability. However, characterizing groundwater flow through fractured bedrock remains challenging due to difficult access and highly heterogeneous geological conditions. In this study, we combined conventional isotopic and hydrochemical analyses with microbial community characterization to investigate groundwater recharge sources and flow paths using a 4‐km‐long horizontal tunnel as a research platform. Results showed that groundwater was recharged by precipitation through independent and inclined fractures, as inferred from the δ18O altitude gradient (−0.25‰ per 100 m, determined from 186 precipitation samples from three stations). Radiocarbon dating revealed millennial‐scale groundwater ages and indicated slow flow velocities in the mountain interior. Where hydrochemical variability was limited at the site scale, microbial communities provided sensitive natural tracers for discriminating groundwater from different fractures. This integrated multi‐tracer framework provides new constraints on groundwater flow pathways and connectivity in fractured systems.

title: Hybrid Seamless Seasonal‐to‐Annual Forecasting for the Wind Energy Sector Over the Americas
content:
Abstract
Wind power generation is sensitive to atmospheric variability across seasonal to annual timescales, creating demand for climate information that is both skilful and temporally consistent. Here we develop a hybrid seamless seasonal‐to‐decadal forecasting framework for annual wind speed over the Americas. The hybrid system combines dynamical predictions from seasonal and decadal forecast systems with a statistical multilinear regression model driven by four large‐scale ocean–atmosphere variability indices. Temporal consistency is achieved by constraining decadal ensemble members according to their agreement with updated seasonal predictions, avoiding discontinuities when transitioning across forecast horizons. Results show that the hybrid framework provides skilful wind predictions in key wind energy regions of the Americas, including the Great Plains and northeastern Brazil, and in some cases outperforms dynamical‐only forecasts, while preserving forecast continuity across timescales. These findings demonstrate the potential of combining seamless dynamical predictions with statistical post‐processing for wind energy climate services.

title: Early Cretaceous Paleomagnetic Constraints on a Smaller Greater India
content:
Abstract
The original extent of Greater India is critical for East Gondwana reconstructions. Recent paleomagnetic results suggest a smaller Greater India at ca. 126 Ma, but the single‐polarity data seriously limit their reliability. We present new petrographic, rock magnetic, and paleomagnetic results from the Jiabula Formation sandstones exposed at the Zhangda section of the northern Tethyan Himalaya. Detrital magnetite is the dominant remanence carrier. Combined with previous limestone data, these results fulfill stringent quality criteria and yield a robust Early Cretaceous paleopole at 9.4°N, 299.5°E (A95 = 1.4°, n = 399), placing the Tethyan Himalaya at 42.9° ± 1.4°S at ca. 126 Ma. Comparison with the expected paleolatitude of India further supports a smaller Greater India. Integrating these results with Campanian data (ca. 75 Ma), we infer a Greater India extent of ∼900 km, refining Early Cretaceous paleogeographic reconstructions. This refined estimate provides a firmer basis for understanding Early Cretaceous paleogeography.

title: Planetary Wave Signatures in F‐Region Electron Density From COSMIC‐2 Global Ionospheric Specification
content:
Abstract
This paper investigates F‐region ionospheric oscillations at planetary wave (PW) periods using electron density (Ne) profiles from COSMIC‐2 Global Ionospheric Specifications (GIS). Recent model studies predicted the presence of PWs in the ionosphere and that half of the variability at PW periods is associated with zonally symmetric (S0) oscillations. The main focus of this paper is to test the model predictions about the Ne variability in PW periods in the F‐region using COSMIC‐2 GIS observations. The derived wavenumber–period spectrum validates the model hypothesis, especially the presence of large S0 oscillations. To isolate PW variability from the lower atmosphere, wavelet filtering is applied at 300 km to minimize solar and geomagnetic effects. Approximately 40% of the F‐region electron density variability in the F‐region is linked to planetary wave activity, demonstrating that, in addition to tides, PWs play an important role in global‐scale plasma variability and ionospheric space weather.
